transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent. We've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. Do you have any questions at all about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for asking. I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that's good to know. Another question I have is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that's helpful. I'm also noticing that I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further.
transcript.delivered: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!
